patch.value: Acceptance criteria are documented as merging like tags but are stored as one delimiter-joined scalar, so concurrent criteria additions from different branches are silently discarded

src/core/item/parse.ts:92 documents applyAcceptanceCriteriaMutations as giving --add-ac/--remove-ac 'tag-API parity' with the explicit promise that 'disjoint additions merge cleanly across branches'. Tags have that property because 'tags' is in ITEM_UNION_COLLECTION_FIELDS and merges by element identity. acceptance_criteria is not in that list: it is stored as a single string joined with '; ', so it takes the scalar three-way path and resolves toward the preferred side like any other scalar. The documented guarantee is therefore false for the one field whose CLI grammar is explicitly list-shaped. Criteria are the field close-validation reads, so the loss is silent in exactly the workflow that is supposed to be enforced.

Concurrent disjoint --add-ac additions on separate branches all survive a merge, or the delimiter-joined scalar semantics are documented at src/core/item/parse.ts, in pm update --help, and in the merge guidance; Every field whose CLI grammar exposes additive and subtractive mutation is either a union collection or is listed as a known-lossy scalar in one enumerable place the merge driver and the docs both read; A merge that discards acceptance criteria names acceptance_criteria and the number of discarded criteria in the receipt guidance rather than reporting a generic scalar conflict
Acceptance criteria are the machine-readable definition of done; losing them on merge silently weakens every close-time check built on them.
Any two agents that add criteria to the same item on different branches lose all but one contribution, and the close validation that reads criteria cannot tell.
Either acceptance criteria merge by element identity like every other list-shaped field, or the docstring and the CLI help state the scalar semantics and pm warns when a merge discards criteria.
The same probe that falsified merge-direction independence falsified this documented guarantee; the fix is small and the loss is unrecoverable.
git merge via pm merge drivers; pm 2026.8.2
Create an item on a base commit, branch three ways, run pm update <id> --add-ac 'criterion from A|B|C' on each branch, commit, then merge all three branches into one clone.
All three disjoint criteria survive, matching the tag-API parity documented at src/core/item/parse.ts:92.

Exactly one criterion survives: acceptance_criteria = 'criterion from A'. The other two appear only as discarded_hash values in the merge receipt. No warning names acceptance_criteria as a lossy field.
